question: Is hypertension associated with chronic kidney disease in US adults?
refined_question: Among noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years; excluding pregnant at examination), is hypertension - ACC/AHA 2017 (BP >=130/80 mm hg or antihypertensive use) associated with a higher prevalence of CKD - eGFR <60 or UACR >=30 mg/g (single measurement), after adjustment for age, sex, race and ethnicity, income-to-poverty ratio, diabetes (self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%), educational attainment, smoking status, and body mass index?
title: Association of Hypertension With Chronic Kidney Disease Among US Adults: NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic
hypothesis: Hypertension - ACC/AHA 2017 (BP >=130/80 mm Hg or antihypertensive use) is associated with a higher prevalence of CKD - eGFR <60 or UACR >=30 mg/g (single measurement).

pico.population: noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years; excluding pregnant at examination)
pico.exposure: Hypertension - ACC/AHA 2017 (BP >=130/80 mm Hg or antihypertensive use)
pico.outcome: CKD - eGFR <60 or UACR >=30 mg/g (single measurement)
pico.covariates: Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Diabetes (self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%), Educational attainment, Smoking status, and Body mass index

outcome.label: CKD - eGFR <60 or UACR >=30 mg/g (single measurement)

exposure.label: Hypertension - ACC/AHA 2017 (BP >=130/80 mm Hg or antihypertensive use)

model.rationale: Binary outcome: survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression with log link estimates prevalence ratios (PRs). PRs are preferred to odds ratios for cross-sectional data because ORs exaggerate associations when the outcome is common (>10%); the quasi-Poisson variance is robust under the design-based (Taylor linearization) estimator. Logistic regression is run as a sensitivity analysis.

adjustment_sets.label: Adjusted for age, sex, and race and ethnicity

missing_data.rationale: Complete-case primary analysis within the design; multiple imputation by chained equations as sensitivity analysis when covariates are missing.

sensitivity.label: Alternative exposure: Hypertension - JNC7 (BP >=140/90 mm Hg or antihypertensive use)

rationale.statistician: Binary outcome: survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression with log link estimates prevalence ratios (PRs). PRs are preferred to odds ratios for cross-sectional data because ORs exaggerate associations when the outcome is common (>10%); the quasi-Poisson variance is robust under the design-based (Taylor linearization) estimator. Logistic regression is run as a sensitivity analysis.
rationale.epidemiologist: Covariates were selected as plausible common causes of hypertension - ACC/AHA 2017 (BP >=130/80 mm hg or antihypertensive use) and CKD - eGFR <60 or UACR >=30 mg/g (single measurement) (minimal confounder set from the domain library): Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Diabetes (self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%), Educational attainment, Smoking status, and Body mass index. Variables on the causal pathway or sharing laboratory components with the outcome/exposure are excluded to avoid over-adjustment.

limitations: Cross-sectional design: temporality cannot be established and associations must not be interpreted causally.
Single measurement of laboratory values; within-person variability and chronicity cannot be assessed.
Residual confounding by unmeasured or imperfectly measured factors (e.g., diet, medications, menstrual blood loss).
Self-reported comorbidities and behaviours are subject to recall and social-desirability bias.
NHANES excludes institutionalized and active-duty military populations.
Operational definition (KDIGO CKD): Chronicity (>3 months) cannot be confirmed from one NHANES visit.
Operational definition (ACC/AHA 2017): BP is the mean of up to 3 readings at a single visit (oscillometric in 2017-2020/2021-2023; auscultatory in earlier cycles - mode differs across cycles).

checks.title: Cross-sectional: temporality cannot be established
checks.detail: Results are reported as associations; causal language is blocked in the manuscript.

checks.title: Approve to hash-lock the protocol before results
checks.detail: SHA-256 of the analysis plan is recorded at approval; any later edit voids the approval. All 5 prespecified sensitivity analyses are reported regardless of result; 5 subgroup/interaction tests are labelled exploratory.

checks.title: Add a named statistician or epidemiologist sign-off
checks.detail: Investigator approval is required to run; journals increasingly expect documented methodological co-authorship for large-database studies.

checks.title: Explicit, same-population comparator
checks.detail: Contrast: participants in the same eligible population without hypertension - acc/aha 2017 (bp >=130/80 mm hg or antihypertensive use). Both groups come from the same probability sample and eligibility criteria (no convenience controls).

checks.title: Outcome includes measured (exam or laboratory) data
checks.detail: Objective measurement captures undiagnosed cases, unlike code-based EHR outcomes.

checks.title: Prespecified adjustment set
checks.detail: Adjusted for 8 covariates. Mediators and definitional overlaps are removed automatically, and an E-value quantifies how strong unmeasured confounding would need to be.

checks.title: A priori hypothesis with literature check
checks.detail: Hypothesis stated before analysis; PubMed/MEDLINE novelty check: 225 PubMed NHANES paper(s) on the full question in 10 years (158 in the last 3), 1 with a title naming the whole question. By element - Hypertension x Chronic kidney disease: 225 NHANES / 7,616 any data.
